[b]Introduction :[/b]
Développé par Red Dot Games et édité par PlayWay, Car Mechanic Simulator 2018 est sorti en juillet 2017. Le concept : gérer son propre garage, diagnostiquer des pannes, démonter et remonter des moteurs pièce par pièce, puis faire fructifier son business en retapant des épaves. Un simulateur de mécanique auto complet, avec plus de 40 modèles de voitures et des milliers de composants.

[b]Ce que j'ai aimé :[/b]
[list]
[*]🔧 Une simulation mécanique étonnamment complète et intuitive : même sans connaissances en mécanique, on comprend vite ce qu'on fait et pourquoi
[*]🚗 Les barn finds et les enchères, une vraie bonne idée : dénicher une épave dans une grange, la restaurer entièrement et la revendre, c'est super satisfaisant
[*]📈 La progression du garage est addictive, on commence dans un atelier minable et on finit à la tête d'un petit empire
[*]🛠️ Le mode expert, sans aucune aide au diagnostic, offre un vrai challenge pour les passionnés de mécanique
[*]💰 Des milliers de pièces détachées et la possibilité de tout revendre pour optimiser ses marges
[/list]

[b]Ce que j'ai moins aimé :[/b]
[list]
[*]🔁 Les missions deviennent répétitives : une vidange par-ci, une panne moteur par-là, les commandes finissent par toutes se ressembler
[*]🏎️ La conduite sur le circuit d'essai est infâme, surtout avec les véhicules puissants
[*]📚 Le tutoriel est mal fichu et vous noie sous les informations sans explication claire
[*]🐛 Le lancement en 2017 a été catastrophique (bugs, sauvegardes perdues), même si le jeu a été largement corrigé depuis
[/list]

[b]Conclusion :[/b]
Après un lancement raté pour lequel Red Dot Games s'est publiquement excusé, CMS 2018 est devenu une référence du genre avec 90 % d'évaluations positives sur Steam. Si visser des boulons virtuels pendant des heures vous détend autant que moi, foncez. C'est répétitif, oui, mais c'est aussi ce qui en fait un excellent jeu de décompression. Recommandé à tous les bricoleurs du dimanche, en promo il est …

(I got a key for this game when they were giving it out for free one week)
Really fun game as someone who is into cars but doesn't spend a lot of time working on them.

Pros:
- farily detailed cars and lots of parts (though not too many parts that are only slightly different)
- parts and repair steps are pretty accurate to real life
- fun building/restoring/puzzle game with some tycoon elements
- very satisfying to restore classic cars
- you'll like it if you like working on cars and have some knowledge about them

Cons:
- didn't find the tutorial very clear at the start, a lot of things weren't obvious (as someone who knows how to do the basics in real life)
- I don't think this game would be easy for someone who knows absolutely nothing about cars, but it would definitely force them to learn about the basics
- jobs can be somewhat repetitive depending on your tolerances and it is a grind to level up enough to get all the shop equipment (though that's part of the point of the game)
- you can drive the cars after you build them but the handling isn't anything special. It's serviceable but didn't blow me away. There's also no proper manually controlled transmission option, which I do greatly prefer.
Game have poor tutorial, at start you have to press garage and do test drive , then actual game begins, this game is pretty fun though

This game sucks, only bought this on sale a couple years ago to make my 9 hours worth it.
--
Mouse and keyboard mappings are confusing and hard to change because the settings cannot be accessed in-game (needing to leave your game to the main menu to do anything to make this ♥♥♥♥ bearable).
--
Taking apart the vehicles are kinda fun, putting them back together as well kinda fun. Intended gameplay is intact.

Morel of the story, don't waste your money on the headache this game gives me when I open it up and have to manually adjust each setting from video to mouse.

A Love Letter to Rust and Wrenches: An Honest Review
Let’s be real for a second: Car Mechanic Simulator 2018 isn't just about fixing digital cars. It’s a therapeutic escape. It’s about that incredible feeling of finally finding that one tiny, 94% worn-out rubber bushing that was causing the whole engine to knock. If you’ve ever spent hours in real life looking for a dropped 10mm socket, this game will speak directly to your soul.

🛠️ The Joy of Getting Your Hands Dirty
The technical depth here is astonishing, but what makes it special is how natural it feels. Taking apart a V8 engine block piece by piece feels like solving a beautiful, greasy puzzle.

•	The Magic: The diagnostic process is genuinely rewarding. Using the compression tester or taking the car to the test track to isolate a suspension issue feels like real detective work.

•	The Grind: Yes, putting back 50 bolts on a cylinder head can test your patience. But honestly? That’s exactly what real mechanic work is. It’s meditative, if you have the right mindset.

🏎️ From a Rusty Garage to a Dream Workshop
The progression captures that classic "started from the bottom" feeling. You begin with barely enough tools to change oil, and eventually, you’re bidding on absolute gems hidden in junk yards or forgotten barns. Restoring a completely rusted muscle car and seeing it shiny on the Dyno is a massive dopamine hit.

📉 The Reality Check: The Driving
We need to talk about the test drives. The driving physics are... well, stiff. It feels a bit like driving a brick on ice. But let’s be honest: we didn’t install this game to compete in Forza. We came here to build, tune, and bring dead engines back to life.

🏆 The Verdict: Is It Worth Your Time?
Absolutely. CMS 2018 has a soul. It respects the car culture and rewards your curiosity. It’s the perfect game to play while listening to a podcast or your favorite music after a long day.


Did this review help you look under the hood?
If this honest breakdown resonated with…

graphically beautiful, easy to get into the rhythm and advance but without adding DLC's can become very repetitive. I have a good amount of hours on the game but like a real mechanic after some tasks I would step away for a smoke, lunch, etc so the hours are a little inflated. 

wishlist: for the older cars in the game you shouldn't be able to buy body/interior bits new, find them in junkyards or barns and repair them if you can. crates should not include parts for cars you do not have the DLC for. Barns and junkyards same and occasionally it would be cool to find high performance or quality bits in a barn to try and repair. the auction is neat but bidding against the bots can be frustrating when they only go back and forth among themselves so far but will drive your price up beyond the value every time. also, it would be cool if you could put one of your cars up for sale in the auction instead of relying on some automatic single calculation of a sale price (but then the bots would very likely lowball you). cut down on the variations for the rims which gets extreme when you take the base number of rims and multiply it by the different sizes (12"-25"). unless you buy new it is nearly impossible to find 4 of the same rim at the same size. the 'custom' bling bits are a nice touch sometimes but being limited to headlights taillights and hoods quickly takes the fun out of it. where's the body kits? 

the only real downside to the game I found was trying to drive the cars. there's no manual transmissions so you can't shift when you want to and if you really powered up the engine then every gear change could send you sideways as the torque breaks traction. you absolutely positively can not drive the cars without a controller and an analog one at that. one race track and solo? that's the perfect inflection point to race your creations against friends so a missed opportunity there(?)

I picked it up on sale and definitely got my money's worth out of it. I might get the 2026 …

A great game if you manage expectations. It's not a substitute for ASE accredited training programs as its a game with a lot of simplifications. It's not a racing game. There are no AI opponents and the driving simulation is not all that..get RevHead instead. What it is for me is a nostalgic replacement for building scale model cars from plastic kits  back in the day with the added bonus of being able to test drive them on in-game provided test, time, and race tracks even though the handling is pretty hit and miss. I also have the 2021 game but I recommend this version especially the CMS 2018 Platinum edition when on steam sale as it has at least 3 or 4 times the car mods in its steam workshop compared to CMS 2021.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe some achievements as an extreme and painful grind, such as requiring tens of thousands of bolt removals or parts examinations.

citations.review_text:
I came to 2018 after playing through Car Mechanic Simulator 2021. The latter is definitely more polished, has a bunch of QoL features that are lacking in 2018 in terms of shopping, parts lists, level progression. Some of the shopping list stuff I'd recommend modding to make it more player-friendly, but I'd still strongly recommend this game as a fun way to relax and unwind while watching something on TV.

My only real complaint is I'm going after the achievements now and I will say that 2018 does feel some of the achievements are purely sadistic - I've logged 122hrs and I've unscrewed 20,000 out of 500,000 bolts for one of the achievements.

Car Mechanic Simulator 2018;

Is a good game for car people, but not a great game for achievement hunters.

The best part is building up cars. Taking an old wreck, stripping it down, replacing parts, fixing the engine, suspension, brakes, bodywork, and then turning it into a finished car is really satisfying. If you are into cars, that side of the game is amazing. The Steam Workshop support also makes it even better because you can mod in your favourite cars and make the garage feel more personal.

The main gameplay loop is fun. You take repair jobs, inspect cars, find broken parts, order replacements, unlock better tools, expand your garage, and eventually restore cars from barns, auctions, and junkyards. Players should keep in mind that this is a repetitive game by design. You are repairing, replacing, rebuilding, and restoring cars over and over, so you need to enjoy that kind of loop to get the most out of it.

The story jobs are a nice idea, but after a few of them they start to feel like long shopping lists instead of fun missions.

The 100% completion is where the game really falls apart for me. The achievements feel like an afterthought, and the grind is ungodly bad. It got to the point where I was using macros overnight just to push progress, which says a lot about how painful the achievement hunt becomes.

I would only recommend Car Mechanic Simulator 2018 to people who love working on cars or enjoy detailed repair sims. As a car-building game, it can be great. As a 100% completion game, it is not worth it.

Do you like CMS 2015? Yes? Reading this review for advice? Then go and buy the game. It's the last one, but better graphics, more detailed gameplay in how to fix things, real life cars in the DLC and the ability to buy cars brand new. Literally the only thing I can fault the devs on is how ridiculous requirements some of the achievements are- examining 10,000 parts springs to mind. I get this weird twinge in my left arm just thinking about it. Who am I kidding, I know I'm getting it eventually... only 9,011 parts left to examine
